           DIPHTHERINUM

         Potentized Diphtheritic Virus


Adapted to patients prone to catarrhal affections of respiratory organs,
        scrofulous individuals. Diphtheria, laryngeal diphtheria,   post-diphtheritic
        paralysis  . Malignancy from the start. Glands swollen; tongue red, swollen; breath
        and discharge very offensive. Diphtheritic; membrane thick, dark. Epistaxis; profound
        prostration. Swallows without pain, but fluids are vomited or returned by the nose.



Relationship.--  Compare:   Diphtherotoxin
        (Cahis) (Chronic bronchitis with rales. Cartier suggests it in the vago-paralytic forms of
        Bronchitis of the aged or in toxic bronchitis after grip).



Dose.--  Thirtieth, two hundredth or C. M potency. Must not be
        repeated too frequently.
